corpus_forum/cf_03_forum_formation_tribu: Every adopting entity must publish a real, working structure for each forum family — not a name on an organization chart. A filer must be able to tell which body handles what.
A published map showing which actual body does the work of each constitutional forum family, and how it is organized — one standing body, several regional ones, or tiers.
Families may share staff, buildings, and software and still must stay constitutionally distinct. Shared plumbing is not a reason to merge functions that are meant to check one another.
Each family needs enough adjudicators and clerical support to actually function, so the same small group is not hearing everything.
A family may create specialized chambers, but the instrument creating one must say which family it sits in and what it covers. A chamber never outranks its family boundary.
Who sits on a chamber, and how they are appointed and serve, must meet the shared floor for delegated binding bodies rather than being arranged case by case.
Each chamber must state up front how its rulings can be reviewed. A chamber may not rewrite routing by habit or quietly take work that belongs to another family.
Creating a specialist chamber requires explaining why ordinary family-level handling will not do. Specialization must be justified, not assumed.
corpus_forum/cf_04_panel_formation_discl: The vocabulary for the rest of the file: what counts as a panel member, and what makes a bench lawful.

Each family must publish its own panel rules in advance — how many members, what counts as quorum, what expertise each seat needs, and who replaces whom. Deciding this after a case arrives invites manipulation.
How members are picked must be public before a case arrives, along with how to object to a given assignment.
Before touching the merits, a proposed member must disclose anything that could reasonably raise a question about impartiality — financial interest, close relationships, prior involvement.
The situations where stepping aside is required rather than optional, including having already acted in the matter in another role.
A usable route for a party to say "this member should not be hearing my case" — in plain language, with a decision that can itself be reviewed.
Recusal cuts both ways. Stepping aside to dodge a politically awkward case, to create delay, or to steer a matter to a preferred substitute is itself misconduct.
Replacements follow a published order rather than being hand-picked for the case, and a substitute carrying the same conflict is no substitute.
What it means when a family genuinely cannot assemble a clean bench — too many conflicts, cascading recusals, capture indicators, or deadlock over composition.
Someone specific and independent must sign the finding that no lawful panel can be formed, and give reasons — otherwise the finding becomes an easy escape hatch.
Once inability-to-form is certified or the lead family is compromised, moving the matter to the backup family is mandatory, not discretionary.
While the fight over who may hear the case continues, a provisional authority may still act — but only to stop irreversible harm, preserve evidence, or protect safety.
The paperwork that lets someone reconstruct later how this particular bench came to hear this particular case.
corpus_forum/cf_05_routing_operations_tr: Every family must publish how it sorts incoming matters by urgency, with at least three levels, and add finer sorting when volume demands it.
Somebody must own the first touch — sorting arrivals into the published classes — and that role carries the same independence and challenge expectations as the rest of the process.
corpus_forum/cf_06_appeal_secondary_revi: Labels stating how far a ruling reaches: only these parties, a whole class, later panels, or a technical standard. Recording the reach prevents a narrow decision from quietly becoming a general rule.
The floor for review: a route that is understandable, usable without unreasonable obstacles, and fast enough to fix a serious error while the remedy still means something.
corpus_forum/cf_07_integrity_safeguards_: How an Integrity forum handles a tangled, multi-part problem: keep one lead record, send each component to the body that properly owns it, and coordinate without absorbing everyone else's jurisdiction.

How a system gets officially recognized as constitutionally aligned within a stated scope, and how that recognition is rechecked later. Recognition is contestable and does not expire into a permanent seal of approval.
The machinery for moving a matter away from a body that cannot judge it impartially — including the severe case where an entire forum family, not just one member, has been compromised.
corpus_forum/cf_08_forum_forensic_analyt: The situations where a forum must be able to call for technical help: the evidence is fragmented, restricted, highly technical, or the uncertainty could change the outcome.
Titles vary — inspector, analyst, special master — but the scope must be written down, and the record must make clear to the parties what that person was asked to do.
Technical helpers face the same conflict screening as decision-makers, and parties must have a real way to challenge who was appointed.
The trail a later reviewer needs: what was tested, how, by whom, what was uncertain, and where the gaps are.
Findings must be understandable to an ordinary affected sentient without dumbing down the technical substance. Acting without notice is allowed only when delay would destroy the evidence.
Two related jobs kept separate: **CF-8** builds the evidence record for one case; contest-integrity monitoring asks whether the system is working across many cases.
corpus_forum/cf_09_independent_investiga: The reasoning in one line: whoever may have caused the problem must not control the investigation into it.
Investigators must sit in a protected line of their own, not under the same command as the enforcement or prosecution they may need to examine.
The authority to take complaints, gather and preserve evidence, interview, and prepare a reasoned packet for whoever decides what happens next.
Several bodies may contribute to one matter, but each stays in its lane — investigating, charging, and deciding must not collapse into a single hand.
No body keeps sole control of an inquiry into its own misconduct. Where the allegations reach the usual investigators, the matter must go elsewhere.
Investigations may sometimes need sealed steps and delayed notice, but secrecy stays bounded by necessity, proportionality, and oversight — it is not a blanket exemption.
The record must state scope, steps, evidence, uncertainty, and reasons — including evidence that cuts against the investigators' own theory — so a closure decision can be checked.
corpus_forum/cf_10_technical_specialist_: Why these bodies exist: to give expert-evidence questions a reviewable home, so expertise informs decisions without becoming an authority no one can question.
Mainly setting and revising the standards other bodies use for expert evidence — reproducibility, uncertainty, replication status, and what counts as sufficient proof.
The specialist chambers an adopting instrument should provide at minimum, such as science, engineering, and medical.
Other domains that may warrant their own chamber where expert-evidence questions recur — ecology, education, statistics, and comparable fields.
Specialist bodies take questions where the expert method is the real dispute. They do not become a general venue by absorbing cases that belong elsewhere.
Published standards must separate what the evidence shows from what someone chose as policy, and must leave room for credible minority and emerging views rather than freezing one school in place.
One body maintains a shared standard; many bodies apply it. Maintenance is centralized so the standard stays coherent, enforcement stays distributed so it stays accountable.
When a technical standard is used against an institution, the case is normally heard by the Institutional family — the standard is technical, but the dispute is about institutional conduct.
Published shared standards bind within their adopted scope. Departing from one requires a justified, recorded variance; treating a standard as merely aspirational is not an option.
A standard already worked out elsewhere is presumptively recognized rather than relitigated from scratch, unless there is a stated reason it does not fit.
In curriculum disputes the question is evidence integrity and honest presentation, not which conclusion the body prefers.
Panels need genuine domain competence plus terms and pay that do not leave members dependent on the funders, journals, or vendors whose work they review.
A specialist body may commission research, but only after publishing a finding that the existing uncertainty is actually blocking reliable decisions.
Where the dispute involves suppressed publication, refused replication, or blocked correction, this file is read together with the institutional rules on scientific publication.
corpus_forum/cf_11_performance_backlog_p: Performance is measured by what an affected party can actually do: find out where the matter stands, reach a forum without unreasonable delay, and challenge a decision while the remedy still matters.
Timing requirements scale with urgency, and they run the whole way through — from first notice to the point where remediation is actually finished, not merely ordered.
The single list of what every forum family must measure and publish. Later sections apply these categories rather than inventing parallel ones.
Each family sets the numbers at which a measure stops being a statistic and becomes an alarm — aging, backlog, accuracy, publication failure, and constitutional risk.
Crossing a threshold obliges an attributable record and a fix, so a breach cannot be absorbed silently into the next reporting period.
Performance must be reviewed on a fixed schedule and compared against earlier periods, so a slow slide is visible before it becomes a crisis.
What the public report must actually show, broken out by family and urgency, so outsiders can see where matters are stuck rather than only a reassuring average.
Independent monitors read the performance data and ask the harder question: do the delays cluster where conflict, capture, or retaliation would predict?

Named failure shapes that are presumed non-compliant — chronic delay concentrated in emergency matters, backlogs that predictably defeat remedy, and unexplained publication delay on significant rulings.
Where a matter involves coercive or containment conditions, forum timing must be checked against the systems-layer floors for lived conditions. Good calendar numbers do not excuse bad conditions.
corpus_forum/cf_12_forum_continuity.md#C: Emergencies may simplify procedure; they may never erase the right to contest, the route to urgent relief, or the record that makes review possible.
The named states a forum can be in, from Normal through Emergency and Fallback to Restoration. Moving between them must be triggered, recorded, and reversible.
A continuity mode switches on only from a documented finding — no lawful panel can be formed, infrastructure is down, key staff are unavailable — not from general unease.
The floor that survives any degraded mode: urgent intake, emergency relief, enough triage to spot Rights-Floor cases, and preservation of the record.
Even in emergency operation the docket must stay identifiable and the evidence chain unbroken, so the period can be reconstructed afterwards.
Parties must be told which mode is active, what still works, and what has been suspended. Silence during a crisis is itself a failure.
When several bodies are affected at once, the plan must name who decides, how evidence is shared, who breaks a deadlock, and in what order normal operation resumes.
Continuity plans must be rehearsed against realistic scenarios — no independent panel available, a backlog surge, an outage — because an untested plan is an assumption.
corpus_forum/cf_13_fallback_operation.md: A smaller panel may sit temporarily only if the rule was written in advance, independence is preserved as far as possible, and a fuller panel reviews rights-affecting decisions promptly.
Each family names its backup in advance, along with how records and review rights travel with a transferred matter. Improvising a venue mid-crisis is what this prevents.
Where the emergency includes suspected capture or concealment, fallback must not leave control inside the suspected chain.
The severe case: a whole family loses control of intake, panels, or publication. The record must state which family, on what basis, and what replaced it.
corpus_forum/cf_14_emergency_adjudicatio: When there is not enough capacity for everything, this is the order: imminent loss of life or irreversible harm first, then evidence about to vanish, then coercive measures needing prompt review.
Emergency powers are rechecked on a schedule while still in force — is the trigger still real, is the simplification still proportionate, is temporary authority hardening into permanent control?
Once the trigger passes, ordinary rules resume, emergency orders that affected rights get reviewed, and delayed records are published or reconstructed.
Every activation ends with findings: what triggered it, what failed, what was used instead, and whether the Rights Floor actually held.
The recognizable abuses — emergency mode extended indefinitely without reauthorization, emergency quorum used to concentrate lasting control, and loss of docket identity or evidence custody.
corpus_forum/cf_15_standard_records_form: The list of records every adopting entity must keep templates for, from intake through backup activation.
What each record must carry — which body, which authority, when, who was responsible, and who was affected — so it remains interpretable years later.
Records are tagged by who may see them: the parties, the public, or restricted review only. Tagging is decided by design rather than case by case.
Evidence must keep its origin, handling history, and transformations attached, whether it is a physical object, a digital file, or a system log.
Publication and retention rules are set in advance and kept consistent with the timeliness, continuity, and emergency requirements elsewhere in this family.
The failures that make later review impossible: action with no attributable record, records omitting the review path, and forms that obscure how a matter was routed.
corpus_forum/cf_16_staffing_reserve_capa: Where the boundaries sit: Chapter Eleven still owns forum architecture, the institutions corpus still owns non-adjudicative governance, and this file adds only the forum-specific staffing layer.
